_comment: Tier-2 for skfem mixed_poisson#4 (previously 'claim inherited -- not yet empirically separated'). Measured on skfem 12.0.1 with the dual mixed RT0/P0 system on MeshTri().refined(3): leaving the outflow facet DOFs free lets the boundary flux settle at whatever the interior dictates, an O(1) deviation from any prescribed value; constraining those DOFs reproduces the prescribed flux to machine precision. NOTE the claim describes the flux trace as the NATURAL condition imposed by a test-side boundary integral -- in the dual mixed form implemented here it is the ESSENTIAL one (constrained RT0 DOFs) while the pressure/Dirichlet datum is the natural one. The observable in the claim's Signal reproduces either way and is what this fixture pins. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 applies the documented fix at the pathology site, replacing the wrong-variant solve that leaves the outflow RT0 facet DOFs free (np.linalg.lstsq on the raw saddle-point block matrix) with the same solve(*condense(K, rhs, x=x, D=outflow)) the right variant uses. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 4 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 makes both fluxes 5.600000 with a 0.000000 gap, removing 'unconstrained_flux_deviates_by_order_one=True' (and raising the forbidden 'FAIL:') so the fixture goes red. FIXED 2026-08-08 (assertion changed). constrained_flux_matches_prescribed was np.allclose(u[outflow], G_PRESCRIBED), i.e. G == G: skfem's solve_linear rebuilds the solution as y = x.copy(); y[I] = <solved interior>, so the constrained DOFs come back holding x byte for byte whatever the physics, the element or the mesh did. It now measures the quantity the claim's Signal names -- the POST-PROCESSED flux. The recovered sigma is interpolated on the outflow facets, sigma . n is integrated, and the mean is compared against the flux density the constraint prescribes: an RT0 facet DOF is the flux THROUGH the facet, so a facet of length h carries mean normal component G/h. Measured unmutated: outflow_facet_length=0.125000, constrained_mean_flux=5.600000, prescribed_mean_flux=5.600000, constrained_flux_relative_error=0.000e+00. WHAT THE NEW LINE CATCHES AND THE OLD ONE COULD NOT, executed 2026-08-08: negate the facet normals in the post-processing (nrm = -fb.normals) -- an orientation/scaling error in exactly the DOF-to-flux relation this line is about. New assertion: constrained_mean_flux=-5.600000, constrained_flux_matches_prescribed=False, FAIL raised, rc=2. Old assertion on the same perturbed run: True, because it never looked at the field. TAUTOLOGY CONTROL on the same perturbed run, recovered forced to True: the expectation survives and rc=0, which is the state the fixture shipped in. HONEST SCOPE: this line is the positive control of the pair, so it does NOT go red under T2_MUTATE=1 -- the mutation fixes the wrong-variant solve, not this one. The pathology probe is unconstrained_flux_deviates_by_order_one, which does. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
